processing_steps_notes.value: Annealing at 550 °C for 9 h, applied only to the 3Cr strip as the annealing-time series (Fig. 11). source.reason: Overall structure of the strips is austenite + ferrite (γ + δ); for the 3Cr strip annealed at 550 °C the dislocation density in austenite decreases with increasing annealing time and the 9 h specimen is imaged in Fig. 11(d).

overall_structure.value: Austenite (γ) matrix with dispersed δ-ferrite second-phase particles (constituent phases remain austenite and ferrite after 550 °C annealing). Annealing at 550 °C progressively reduces the dislocation density in the austenite with increasing annealing time, while the κ-carbide superlattice in the austenite remains very weak in the Cr-containing strip.

purpose.value: Measure the mechanical properties of the 3Cr strip after 9 h annealing at 550 °C as part of the annealing-time series

key_findings.value: Plasticity of the 3Cr strip increases gradually with annealing time; the 9 h curve reaches the largest strain (~50%) among the 3Cr series, while the yield strength does not change significantly after 1 h annealing.

unmapped_findings: For the 3Cr strip annealed at 550 °C, κ-carbides are mainly precipitated in the first hour of annealing while recovery (removal of dislocations) requires longer time; longer annealing time may coarsen κ-carbides, so the annealing time should be optimized to balance κ-carbide coarsening and dislocation-density reduction (block b0050).

The plasticity of the 3Cr strip increases gradually with increasing annealing time at 550 °C, but the yield strength does not change significantly after 1 h annealing; the 9 h annealing is the longest time in this series (block b0050).

The 550 °C heat treatments were carried out in a vacuum electric resistance furnace and only the 3Cr alloy was used for the different-annealing-time series (Fig. 11); the 5 h/550 °C data and the tensile table values (YS/UTS/TE) reported elsewhere in the paper belong to the 5 h process, not to this 9 h sample (blocks b0018, b0049).
